t: Windward commission recommends against Hawaii County data center bill over vague definition
b: The commission voted 5-1 to send an unfavorable, non-binding recommendation on Bill 170, mainly because the data center definition was not specific enough. Members generally supported the intent. The Leeward commission and county council still must weigh in.
iw: Unfavorable recommendation lowers near-term odds of the ban passing as written.

t: Windward Planning Commission defers Hawaii County data center ban until October
b: The commission voted 4-0 to postpone action on Bill 170. The planning director backed the distinction but suggested a 10,000-square-foot threshold, with larger facilities needing a use permit. Commissions must send recommendations to the council by November 4.
iw: Delay prolongs uncertainty over a possible ban but keeps it unresolved.

t: Hawaii County council committee advances Bill 170 barring industrial-scale data centers
b: A county council committee unanimously forwarded Bill 170, which would separate data centers from allowed data processing facilities and make industrial-scale data centers an impermissible use. Facilities serving public institutions and an existing Kawaihae site would be unaffected.
iw: Proposed countywide ban on industrial-scale data centers would block new projects.
